newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ALP CALLS FOR $14 A WEEK RISE FOR LOW PAID
A submission to the Living Wage case by the A-L-P has called for an annual safety net wage rise for low-paid workers half way between what the A-C-T-U's demanding, and the Government's offering.
Shadow Industrial Relations Minister, Bob McMullan, handed the submission, calling for a rise of at least 14 dollars a week, to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission today.
Mr McMullan has also asked for a review of minimum award rates, and safeguards, to ensure part-time workers don't miss out on over-award payments and superannuation.
NEW MAP WILL HELP MINERAL EXPLORATION COMPANIES
The Federal Government has launched a new geological map of Australia which will assist mineral exploration companies in their search for deposits.
The magnetic map, which is based on 45 years of aerial surveys, reveals features of rock formations up to 20 kilometres below the surface.
Resources and Energies Minister Warwick Parer says the new technology is essential considering most large mineral deposits protruding to the surface have been found.
Senator Parer says the 75 million dollar cost of producing the map is an investment in Australia's 40 billion dollar mining exports industry.
YELDHAM WAS "ON SIDE" WITH POLICE
The New South Wales Police Royal Commission is hearing new claims that the late Judge David Yeldham was "on side" with the Police Department.

A former transit policeman, testifying from an undislcosed location overseas, says he and his partner arrested two men emerging from one toilet cubicle at Sydney's Central Railway Station on the 12th of December, 1988.
The witness says he let both men walk but reported the matter to his superiors.
Some days later, he says, he was told the Police Department knew Mr Yeldham was homosexual, that he was "on side" and wasn't one of those judges who disliked police.
NSW ABORIGINAL LEGAL SERVICE FACES FURTHER SCRUTINY
Allegations that the New South Wales Aboriginal Legal Service has misspent money given to it by ATSIC have been referred to the Federal Police and the Taxation Commissioner.
Federal Aboriginal Affairs Minister, John Herron, announced the move after an investigation by the Australian Securities Commission.
In November, ATSIC ceased funding the service, and is now trying to recover over 900-thousand dollars from it.
REPUBLICAN MOVEMENT WANTS PLEBISCITE
The Australian Republican Movement says the Opposition's proposal for a plebiscite next year on the republic is an ideal way to find out what the public wants.
The Opposition wants a plebiscite to be followed by a parliamentary inquiry and a referendum if Australians vote in favour of a republic.
Republican Chair Malcolm Turnbull says a People's Convention will be useful only if the participants are elected, otherwise it'll be a politicians' convention and won't have any legitimacy.
He's urging the Federal Government to take up the Opposition's suggestion.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
